div.head: ECf 32 C 1
div.ab: Guti uero similiter cum ueniunt, suscipi debent et protegi in regno isto sicut coniurati fratres nostri et sicut propinqui et proprii ciues regni huius: exierunt enim quondam de nobili sanguine Anglorum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 658 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 C …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

note.seg: wohl nicht Deutsche Kaufleute Gothlands, die England 1237 privilegirte, sondern Jüten als Vertreter der Dänen, die im 12. Jh. Londonern gleich standen; Höhlbaum III S. 389; Steenstrup Danelag 380; Johann privilegirt 1208 Schiffe aus Denemargia et Norweia; Rot. lit. Patent. p. 83. Auch Will. Malm. Reg. II 116 legt Anglia vetus inter Saxones et Gothos. Ähnliches sagt der Londoner von Norwegern 32 E 3 f.

probably not the German merchants of Gotland, whom England privileged in 1237, but Jutes as representatives of the Danes, who in the 12th century stood equal with Londoners; Höhlbaum III p. 389; Steenstrup, Danelag 380; John privileges ships from Denemargia et Norweia in 1208; Rot. lit. Patent. p. 83. Will. Malm., Reg. II 116, too places Anglia vetus inter Saxones et Gothos. The Londoner says something similar of the Norwegians, 32 E 3 f.
sicut homines proprii werden Fremde begünstigt in Freibriefen, so seit 1157 Cölner; Höhlbaum Hansisch. Urk. I S. 8. 16. 22
foreigners are favoured sicut homines proprii in charters, so from 1157 the men of Cologne; Höhlbaum, Hansisch. Urk. I pp. 8. 16. 22
unde Co Or; n. et fehlt Ld
unde Co Or; n. et lacking in Ld

div.ab: Likewise the Guti (Goths [?]), when they come, ought to be received and protected in this kingdom as our sworn brothers and as kinsmen and own citizens of this kingdom: for they went out once from the noble blood of the English.

note.seg: Wie I 658*, gegen Gl 'Gotland' [das Verf. u. 32 E erwähnt] n. 2, mein ich nun, dass Verf. nicht an Gotländer, sondern an Jüten dachte. Seine ursprüngliche Lesart nämlich lautet wie Rs: sanguine Saxonum Germannie, scilicet de sanguine Anglorum. Unzweifelhaft liegt eine, freilich wohl nur mittelbare, Erinnerung an Bæda vor. Zum Dänisch-Engl. Handel vgl. A. Bugge in Reallex. Germ. Altt. 429. 432f., der jedoch Guti: 'Gotländer' deutet; Englands Verkehr mit Insel Gotland um 1200 behandelt er in Zs. Lübeck. Gesch. 18 (1916) 115

As in I 658*, against Gl 'Gotland' [which the author mentions below, 32 E] n. 2, I now think that the author was thinking not of Gotlanders but of Jutes. For his original reading runs as in Rs: sanguine Saxonum Germannie, scilicet de sanguine Anglorum. Undoubtedly there is a recollection, admittedly probably only indirect, of Bede. On Danish-English trade cf. A. Bugge in Reallex. Germ. Altt. 429. 432f., who however interprets Guti as 'Gotlanders'; England's traffic with the island of Gotland about 1200 he treats in Zs. Lübeck. Gesch. 18 (1916) 115
